home.aboutIntro: I did my master's in Information Management at NKUST, working somewhere between UI/UX design and human factors. As a data analysis intern at e-Excellence, I kept coming back to one question: how do you get a dashboard full of numbers to just tell you what matters? An exchange year in Computer Science at THWS in Germany then showed me how differently people read the same button depending on where they grew up. For my thesis, I took on Taiwan's OSCE medical assessment system and used user-centered design to untangle its back-office workflows. Drawing the new flow was the easy part. Getting it adopted is the work I'm still pushing on.
home.aboutResearch: Most of my research comes back to one idea: bringing human factors into clinical settings. It began in 2023 with a gesture-controlled AR ordering interface, then moved into hospitals, where I used eye tracking and usability testing on a medication recognition system. The projects changed; the question didn't. When the pressure is high and there's little room for error, can an interface spare someone one more mistake?
beyondGridParagraphs: When I'm not nudging pixels or digging through data, I'm usually drawing. The two never stay apart for long. Halfway through a web page a character pops into my head, and more often than not it ends up living on that page.

I've been a student ambassador, an international volunteer, and for a while a resident of Würzburg. Living somewhere new means relearning the small things, like buying bread or catching a tram, and once the ordinary stops being obvious, you start actually seeing it. For a designer, that's a pretty good trade.

portfolio.eyebrow: Somewhere between technical logic and human intuition.
portfolio.headline: Portfolio
portfolio.intro: Honestly, what hooks me isn't how things look. It's how people actually work. So I design from evidence: eye tracking, emotional responses, user interviews, all pointed at one question — does this layout actually help? Some weeks that means tearing apart a chaotic technical interface; some nights it's trying the same dark-mode gray over and over. Big job or small, the goal doesn't change: find where people get stuck, and get it out of their way.

gallery.intro: A good photo starts with a story. I move between film and digital — film makes me slow down, digital lets me take the extra frame. This is the archive: ongoing projects, places along the way, and days I did not edit much :)
